about: Chord-fit measurements of the unprocessed sung melody of v2_2 for harmony designer A (I, IV, V7 only). All shares are fractions of the voiced sung time (44.85 s = 8970 frames of 5 ms in the kept syllables of 7 verses), evaluated at each frame's own time in the new song form (placement shifts of kesim.json, no time-stretch).

metric_definitions.chord_tone: sung pitch class is a chord tone of the chord on that beat
metric_definitions.scale_non_chord: in the key's scale but not a chord tone
metric_definitions.outside_scale: not in the key's scale (and not a chord tone); chord_tone + scale_non_chord + outside_scale = 1
metric_definitions.clash_any: not a chord tone AND (a semitone above or below a chord tone OR a tritone from the chord root)
metric_definitions.clash_sustained: the part of clash_any inside a clash run longer than 150 ms; a run survives up to 60 ms without sung pitch (a consonant) and up to 15 ms of non-clash frames; run length = last - first frame + 5 ms
metric_definitions.clash_sustained_strict: same without any bridging (consecutive 5 ms frames only)
metric_definitions.consonant_non_chord: scale_non_chord that is not a clash
metric_definitions.sounding_semitone: PHYSICAL, from the band model (bant.py, checked note for note against midi/altyapi_C.mid): share of the sung time during which a band note one semitone away in pitch class is really sounding (note-on .. note-off + 30 ms). In the oom-pah pattern the third and seventh of a chord sound on the off-beats and on beats 1 and 3, not on beats 0 and 2.
metric_definitions.sounding_semitone_sustained: the part of sounding_semitone in runs longer than 150 ms (same run rule)
metric_definitions.V: the dominant as a plain triad = the V7 of the task with its seventh left out of the BAND (the singer sings that seventh). Chord-level numbers of a plan written with V treat the seventh as a non-chord tone; the same plan written with V7 treats it as a chord tone.
metric_definitions.modes: 'note' (primary): a frame carries the pitch class of the note it belongs to (kesim.json syllable.notes; scoops and glides count with their note). 'frame': every 5 ms frame is rounded on its own (16.9 % of the frames are then in transit between notes). 'chords_40ms_early': note mode with all chord changes 40 ms earlier (the singer starts syllables 20-70 ms before the beat).

sade_shape_rules.T2: the dominant is followed by the dominant or I, never by IV
sade_shape_rules.T3: bar 6 ends on the dominant or I
sade_shape_rules.ties: J within 0.005: fewer chord changes, then fewer changes on beats 1 / 3

reference_original_d_minor_loop.scale: D natural minor + C# (the leading tone inside the A chord)
reference_original_d_minor_loop.note_on_reading: chord-level metrics only (the original band is not the oom-pah band, so no 'sounding' numbers). tempo.json notes that the A chord of the original has a weak third and a D on top in its last beat (Asus4 / anticipation); against a plain A major triad the sung D of 'var' / 'Baba'nin' counts as a clash here.

robustness_of_the_chosen_bars.about: the best sade-shaped bars of key C recomputed under other pitch readings, with chord changes 40 ms earlier, with each verse left out and for each verse alone

key_ranking_robustness.about: score and bars of the best plan per key for weights w = 1, 2, 4 in J = chord_tone - w * (clash_sustained + outside_scale)
